body:
PROPOSED P0 SUCCESSOR MIGRATION after both exact-SHA blocks; no repository edit yet.

Seam sweep. Exact diff e584ad6..6a21892 adds eight qualified-private production doors: the three SupportAssessment constructors; assessedFromWire, unestablished, and notApplicable; CostBreakdown.external; and CostBreakdown.unassessable. A temp downstream source in package storymodel4s.align.attack reached all eight, directly built Assessed(NaN), directly built both reason cases, accepted assessedFromWire(0.5,{Semantic}), built external total NaN, and built unassessable from the invalid assessed value. It compiled successfully. Source SHA-256 499181dafd036792f07ccee04a0f288273745fc198f2924d8167c89c076ae50a. The three new private[wog] helpers are test-source platform/file readers, not constructors or shipped artifact authority; I propose no production migration for them.

Recommended type shape. Assessed must carry canonical measuredTerms plus canonical eligibleWeights, not only eligible term names. Its share is computed in enum order from those fields. Unestablished carries the same evidence; EmptyEligibility is derived only from an empty eligible-weight map and ZeroEligibleWeight only from a nonempty all-zero map. All concrete constructors become bare private. The sole evidence factory validates finite nonnegative weights, measured subset of eligible, nonempty positive denominator for Assessed, and derives the variant, reason, and share. NotApplicable remains nonnumeric and is admitted only as the external or unreachable singleton checked against the enclosing record.

Wire shape. Keep hsmm/v4 because no v4 artifact has landed. Assessed wire records measuredTerms, eligible term weights, and the derived share; Unestablished records the same derivation evidence and derived reason. Decode recomputes from the evidence and refuses any tag, reason, or share that differs bit-for-bit from the result. It never calls an unchecked assessedFromWire or caller-selected reason factory. AlignWire also requires measuredTerms to equal terms.keySet minus imputedTerms and every priced term to be eligible. External and unreachable rows retain no numeric support evidence. This changes only already-authorized cost, wire, codec, tests, v4 golden, and golden courts.

Construction boundary. Remove every newly added qualified-private production door. SupportAssessment uses bare-private constructors plus checked public evidence construction. CostBreakdown.external becomes a finite-nonnegative checked factory used through GraphHsmm error propagation. CostBreakdown.unassessable takes derivation inputs and can only compute zero or unestablished support; it no longer accepts a support value. The pre-existing CostBreakdown case-class door can still join a valid support value to a false record. My recommendation is either explicit approval to seal CostBreakdown as a non-case class in this same cost.scala/WireSuite slice, or a hard landing dependency on bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX. Without one of those, the wire path is checked but the published Scala record remains forgeable.

Courts. Add downstream storymodel4s.align.attack and unrelated consumer-package compile refusals for direct constructors and all removed rehydration helpers; positive controls for each door; runtime wire mutations for all-measured share not 1, no-measured share not 0, changed eligible weight, changed measured term, changed reason, and changed tag; and a mutation opening each constructor/factory that the refusal court kills. Re-run the exact reference-scope gate and existing JVM, JS, Native support courts. Preserve the separate Native fresh-inference 1-ULP qualification.

Documentation. I recommend no path expansion here. Add an explicit landing-order dependency on bd-01M1D214VVRE118RTEQQ09P7SA so codec/README.md and ADR 0001 cannot still claim hsmm/v1 when this v4 successor lands.

Chief: please choose CostBreakdown sealing now versus the explicit bd-01M17ZN dependency, confirm the same 12 changed-path envelope, and record the docs dependency. I will then recut one immutable successor addressing both reviews.
